## Download

Download **`Rastro-windows-x64.exe`** below and run it. There's nothing to install. Windows will probably warn you the first time because the file isn't signed yet: click **More info → Run anyway**. The [README](https://github.com/MaxSala/rastro-tarkov#is-it-safe) explains why, and how to check the file yourself.

Already using Rastro? Close it and replace the old `.exe` with this one. Your settings, points, maps, prices and quest progress are kept. To get the hideout and the bosses, open **Quests** and download the data again (the refresh button).

## What's new

**Hideout** (`Ctrl+5`)
- Set the level of each station and see what the next one asks for: items, other stations, trader loyalty, skills and build time.
- Station requirements turn green as your hideout meets them. Levels are kept per game mode, like your quests.
- **Items** now adds up quests and hideout: what both still ask for, for the next level or for every level left. The Market's item card says which stations need it, so you know not to sell it.

**Bosses on the map**
- A new **Bosses** layer: where each boss can appear and the chance of meeting it right there.
- Hover for the zone, escorts and when it arrives; click to see every spawn point of the zone.
- Chances follow your game mode, since PvP and PvE differ.

**Raid clock**
- In the menu, the top bar shows the time in Tarkov on both sides, so you can pick day or night before queueing.
- In a raid: time left and, from your last screenshot, the time in your raid.
- Click it for the details: when the raid ends, the armored train window on Reserve and Lighthouse, and the bosses of the map.

Spawn chances and positions come from [tarkov.dev](https://tarkov.dev). Train timings follow the Escape from Tarkov wiki. Tarkov time uses the same formula as [tarkov-time](https://github.com/adamburgess/tarkov-time) (MIT).

Full history in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/MaxSala/rastro-tarkov/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
